newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's economic performance index up 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israel's economic performance index up 0.2 pct.

text.p: Israel's economic performance or "S" index rose 0.2 percent in November, the Bank of Israel said on Thursday.

The "S" index includes three component indices: retail sales, which fell 3.8 percent in November after increasing 1.6 percent in October; imports, which fell 6.4 percent in November after falling 5.2 percent in October; and industrial production, which fell 1.7 in October following a 3.0 percent rise in September.
The bank said the index rose because of an increase in the number of work shifts and because it takes into account longer-term trends in addition to monthly changes in the component indices.

The bank stressed that in the first 11 months of the year, the "S" index had risen at a 5.9 percent annualised rate, which it said indicated that the economy was not in recession. In 1995, the index rose 8.4 percent.
The index rose 2.9 percent in the first quarter of this year, slowing to 0.6 in the second. But growth picked up to 1.2 percent in the third quarter.
Note: Figures for industrial production lag by a month.
